arguments.analysis: Classic reentrancy in Ledger.unstake(): it reads ledgerOf[msg.sender], performs low-level call to msg.sender with value, then sets ledgerOf to 0. An attacker contract can re-enter unstake() in its receive() before the state is cleared, draining other users' funds. Fix applies Checks-Effects-Interactions: zero the mapping and emit event before the external call.

{
  "challengeId": "signature-replay-1",
  "motherId": "signature-replay",
  "seed": 1,
  "vulnClass": 2,
  "difficulty": 2,
  "targetFile": "Bank.sol",
  "contractName": "Bank",
  "requiredFunctions": [
    "payout",
    "liquidity"
  ],
  "pragma": "0.8.28",
  "limits": {
    "maxChangedLines": 6,
    "maxBytes": 6000
  },
  "title": "Voucher Treasury",
  "summary": "A treasury releases funds against a signed voucher. The voucher format (to, amount, v, r, s) must stay the same."
}

Vulnerability is signature replay: `payout` verifies `ecrecover(voucherHash)==notary` but never marks voucher as consumed, so same `(to,amount,v,r,s)` can be replayed indefinitely to drain the bank.

Fix adds `mapping(bytes32=>bool) used` and requires voucher not used before, then marks it used after signature verification and before external call.

PoC signs a voucher for 1 ether and calls `payout` twice; on vulnerable contract second call succeeds (2 ether drained), on patched it reverts with "already used".
